paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God means every word He says, the good AND the hard. He lays out two roads and tells them plainly where each one goes. Walk with Him, and He says, "I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people" (Leviticus 26:12). Turn away, and the road gets harder with every step (Leviticus 26:14-18).

Now, that's a heavy sermon, and I'm not going to rush past it. I think the heaviest part is that the LORD keeps speaking even when they keep refusing. More than once He says "if in spite of all this you do not obey Me…", which tells me He is not hunting for a reason to be done with them (Leviticus 26:27; see also 26:18, 23). When He names what they won't accept, He calls it "My discipline" (Leviticus 26:23), and I think that shows how serious sin is to Him and how much He wants His people to come back.

And that's where the sermon lands, and it's the part I'd tape to my oven door. Even in the land of their enemies, the LORD says, "I will not reject or despise them so as to destroy them and break My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God" (Leviticus 26:44). If they confess and humble their hearts, He says He will remember His covenant with Jacob, Isaac and Abraham (Leviticus 26:40-42). So when you drift, baker, don't hide in the back and gather dust like I did in that drawer. Confess it, turn around, and come home, because He is a God who keeps His promises.
